America.title: CONTINUATION: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop after an hours-long halt; officials blame overloaded legacy air traffic communications equipment and say there is no indication of a cyberattack
America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; Transportation Secretary Duffy said Saturday officials see 'zero evidence' the disruption was caused by a cyberattack or related to AI systems (Global News). Viral posts claiming a coordinated cyberattack have no supporting evidence; Reuters headline says the US aviation shutdown is blamed on an L3Harris-installed router; FirstSquawk relays CNBC that the FAA says its investigation has not yet identified the cause, and relays NYT that disruptions continue after 9,000 Friday cancellations and 5,000 Saturday delays; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: UPDATE: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; Posts report heavy clashes for a second night along the Sheraro–Badme border between the Ethiopian army and Eritrean forces backed by Tigray Defense Forces; journalist Simon Ateba reports the United States warned Ethiopia and Eritrea against a new war as clashes multiply; still no official statement from either government found in posts checked

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. Another post reports more than 50 Orthodox Christians killed in an attack on a village in the Arsi region, following attacks it says killed at least 60 last month, so the figures may describe different attacks. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Reuters Africa separately reports Africa's top public health agency saying attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo that has killed more than 5,400 people. The 66 figure was not confirmed by a primary WHO or UN post in posts checked.
Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Armed thugs attack opposition NDC town hall meeting in Lagos, Nigeria
Africa.summary: TheCable reports thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos on Thursday (Nov. 12). A commentator relaying News Central TV says vehicles were destroyed and shots were fired into the air, and NDC supporters blame ruling-party (APC) thugs, which is unverified.

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: ADF attacks reportedly kill at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
Africa.location: Mambasa territory, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Africa.summary: Civil-society monitors say Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels killed at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory between Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov. 10–11) and abducted at least 10 people, according to posts from Salone Messenger and NewsTongue. The attacks come amid the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo.
Africa.status: Early reports citing civil-society monitors; no Congolese army or government statement found on X in posts checked; CGTN Africa, citing humanitarian and security sources quoted by AFP, reports at least 44 civilians killed this week in a series of attacks by Islamic State-linked ADF fighters across northeastern DR Congo; it is unclear how much of that count overlaps with the Mambasa figures; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Fire and explosion at Sirte Oil Company gas complex in Marsa Brega, Libya, kills one worker; production unaffected
Africa.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation says one worker was killed and four injured after a fire triggered an explosion at Sirte Oil Company's gas complex in Marsa Brega on Wednesday (Nov. 11), but gas and crude production was unaffected, Reuters and Arab News report. CGTN Europe says the NOC attributes it to an explosion in a fuel gas line and that the fire was contained.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (NOC); fire contained; appears accidental, no indication of an attack in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Casablanca power outage — power restored; Moroccan outlets attribute it to wind gusts and storms (Storm Charles), and L'Economiste cites an incident on very-high-voltage lines
Africa.location: Casablanca and Nouaceur province (Bouskoura, Dar Bouazza), Morocco
Africa.summary: A large power outage hit many Casablanca neighborhoods and nearby localities on Wednesday afternoon (Nov. 11), starting around 5 p.m. local time, according to Yabiladi, Le Desk, Maroc Hebdo and state broadcaster SNRT. Medi1 TV reports wind gusts and storms caused the outage, L'Economiste reports an incident on very-high-voltage lines, and Le360 says power was fully restored around 9 p.m. in the affected neighborhoods, attributing the outage to Storm Charles. State news agency MAP and SNRT, citing prefecture sources, reported power restored in several zones earlier in the evening.
Africa.status: Power reported restored (fully, per Le360); regional utility SRM Casablanca-Settat issued an official statement (relayed by Medias24 and Maroc Hebdo); cause attributed to weather and a very-high-voltage line incident by multiple outlets; the earlier cyberattack hypothesis is not supported by any official source in posts checked; situation appears stabilized, can move to routine coverage; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.location: Manso Keniago (Amansie South District), Ashanti Region, Ghana
Africa.summary: A confrontation broke out on Wednesday (Nov. 11) between personnel of Ghana's National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents and suspected illegal miners as the task force removed seized excavators at Manso Keniago. Africa.summary: Reuters, citing police and a senior regional official, reports eight people — two police reservists, five construction workers and a driver — were killed Tuesday in northeast Kenya near the Somali border in an attack by suspected al-Shabaab militants. Africa.summary: Reuters reports nearly 64,000 people have fled northern Nigeria for neighbouring Niger this year, escaping attacks by Islamist militants and armed gangs, according to the UN refugee agency. It says the arrivals add to mounting humanitarian needs in Niger.
Africa.status: UN agency figure via Reuters; ongoing displacement; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudan: UNICEF says 15 power stations hit in October as drone strikes spread; rights group says RSF drone attack on displaced people in Blue Nile's Al-Kurmuk killed 16
Africa.summary: UN News reports UNICEF's James Elder said 15 power stations were hit in October alone as long-range drone strikes and drought threaten survival in Sudan. Arab News reports the UN says two thirds of children killed or injured in Sudan this year were victims of drone strikes. Wasl News reports an RSF drone attack killed nine civilians in a Blue Nile village on Tuesday; that toll is not independently confirmed.

Africa.location: Mogadishu to Barawe corridor, Lower Shabelle, Somalia
Africa.summary: Somali Guardian reports a Ugandan military convoy of more than 70 vehicles took over a week to travel from Mogadishu to Barawe as part of the withdrawal of remaining Ugandan troops, delayed by al-Shabaab attacks. Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya Red Cross says Moyale border clashes in Ethiopia have displaced more than 50,000 people
Africa.summary: Voice of Horn reports Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan says clashes around Ethiopia's Moyale area have displaced more than 50,000 people, many into northern Kenya, with shortages of food, shelter and bedding. South America.summary: Ecuador's interior minister, John Reimberg, has warned of an alleged plan to attack President Daniel Noboa, which a local outlet says he linked to a criminal leader known as 'Loco Ovidio' and the ELN. Colombian broadcaster La FM interviewed Reimberg about the alleged plot.

South America.location: Desepaz, eastern Cali, Valle del Cauca, Colombia

South America.title: CONTINUATION: Remedios de Escalada (Lanús) gas explosion — five remain critical with severe burns, new gas leaks found and search of rubble continues for a missing MetroGAS worker
South America.location: Coronel Beltrán and Del Valle Iberlucea, Remedios de Escalada, Lanús, Buenos Aires province, Argentina
South America.summary: A machine damaged a gas distribution pipe during MetroGAS network-renewal work on Friday morning, causing an explosion and a large fire that destroyed a shop in the commercial centre. The Lanús municipality says 20 people were injured, five of them seriously, and taken to Hospital Evita. Local media report evacuations of a nearby care home and school.
South America.status: Official statement issued (Lanús municipality; MetroGAS statement); injury counts vary between outlets (some report up to 27); cause attributed to damage during gas works; Lanús civil-defense director Claudio Arale says a body, not yet identified, was recovered and two MetroGAS workers are missing, per Infobae; Corta reports one dead, 30 injured and two missing; Rosario3, citing Arale, says the gas leak was still not controlled more than seven hours after the blast; El País (Uruguay) and El Canciller report one dead and 30 or more injured; El Canciller says residents and the Lanús municipality blame MetroGAS, which had outsourced the works, and that two executives have been detained (not confirmed by an official post found); On Saturday Clarín, citing Buenos Aires provincial health sources, reports five people remain hospitalized in serious condition on mechanical ventilation with burns over 40-90% of their bodies (Radio Mitre also reports five critical). El Canciller reports two new gas leaks in the blast zone as MetroGAS works on site, with debris removal under way and police dogs searching the rubble for possible victims. DataDiario reports the search continues for MetroGAS worker Marcelo García, 47, missing since the blast; DataDiario reports another gas leak about 500 meters from the blast site, on Melo street in the 4000 block, with neighbors evacuated; carried forward from 6:15 PM ET, no newer change found

South America.location: Siloé / El Lido area, near the Escuela de Carabineros, southwest Cali, Colombia

Middle East.status: Single established outlet found on X this window; no Israeli military statement found; figures not independently verified; Reuters, citing medics, confirms an airstrike on a Sabra metal foundry killed three and four more were killed elsewhere in Gaza City and Khan Younis; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Heavy rain floods more than 70,000 tents in Gaza, killing four Palestinians including three children
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera reports heavy rain flooded more than 70,000 tents in Gaza, killing four Palestinians, including three children. US Senator Brian Schatz urged Israel to allow building materials, rescue equipment and winter supplies in.
Middle East.status: Reported by Al Jazeera; no UN or local authority post checked directly; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UAE retailer Landmark Group investigates unauthorised access to its Shukran loyalty programme
Middle East.summary: Landmark Group says it is investigating a cyber incident involving unauthorised access to its Shukran loyalty programme, The National reports. Customer information involved includes names, contact details and dates of birth.
Middle East.status: Company statement reported by The National; number of affected customers not given; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Israeli settlers set fire to a vehicle scrapyard in al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya, south of Nablus; more than 100 vehicles destroyed
Middle East.location: al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya, south of Nablus, occupied West Bank
Middle East.summary: Arab News reports that Israeli settlers set fire to a vehicle scrapyard in the Palestinian village of al-Lubban ash-Sharqiya on Wednesday (Nov. 11), destroying more than 100 vehicles. Anadolu Arabic reports Hamas described the burning of more than 100 Palestinian vehicles and other property as a terrorist attack.
Middle East.status: Early reports; no casualties reported in posts checked; no Israeli police or military statement found on X in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: RSF reported to have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud, West Kordofan, Sudan, amid a citywide communications blackout
Africa.summary: Anadolu Agency and TRT Afrika, citing the local Dar Hamar Emergency Committee, report that Sudan's Rapid Support Forces have killed 10 civilians in Al-Nuhud since Thursday. The committee reports home raids, looting and a citywide communications blackout.
Africa.status: Two state-backed outlets citing a local relief group; no RSF response or independent confirmation found on X; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Construction-site perimeter wall collapse in Riverside, Nairobi, kills at least three; toll reported as six
Africa.summary: A perimeter wall at a construction site in Riverside, Nairobi, collapsed on Nov. 14, killing three people per Citizen TV, with more workers believed trapped. KBC and Eastleigh Voice report 11 injured taken to hospital, and NTV shows Kenya Red Cross recovering victims. A post citing the Daily Nation says the toll has risen to six and the search continues.
Africa.status: Confirmed by Kenyan broadcasters; the six-dead figure is relayed from Daily Nation and not confirmed by officials on X; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least 44 civilians reported killed in Islamic State-linked ADF attacks in eastern DR Congo
Africa.location: Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (exact localities not given)
Africa.summary: Sitrep Africa reports at least 44 civilians were killed in attacks by the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in DR Congo. The post gives no locality, dates or source, and it is unclear whether this overlaps earlier reported ADF attacks in Mambasa territory.
Africa.status: Single-source early report; no Congolese army, MONUSCO or local official confirmation found on X; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: More than 50 reported killed in clashes between vigilantes and armed gangs in Zamfara, Nigeria
Africa.location: Zoma village, Gummi area, Zamfara State, northwest Nigeria
Africa.summary: Residents told AFP that more than 50 people were killed in clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes in Zamfara state. They said vigilantes in Zoma village ambushed bandits on Thursday after the gang kidnapped people from nearby Gummi district.
Africa.status: Early reports (AFP, citing residents, relayed by PakTV Global); no police or state government confirmation found on X; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: At least eight reported killed in dawn raid on Malkamari village near the Ethiopia–Kenya border
Africa.location: Malkamari, Dawa Zone, Ethiopia (opposite Banisa, Mandera County, Kenya)
Africa.summary: Kenyan security-news account InsecurityKE reports gunmen raided Malkamari, on the Ethiopian side of the border, early Saturday while residents slept, killing at least eight people including women and children. Nomad TV Kenya carries the same initial count, and burials are reported at Alo Birti village near the border.
Africa.status: Early reports; no Ethiopian or Kenyan government statement found in posts checked; attackers not confirmed; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Sudanese army says it shot down a hostile long-range drone that crossed from Ethiopia into Blue Nile region
Africa.location: Dandaro area, Blue Nile region, Sudan (Ethiopia border)
Africa.summary: Addis Standard reports Sudan's army said its air defences shot down a long-range drone it described as hostile in the Dandaro area of Blue Nile region on Friday, alleging it crossed from Ethiopia. The report adds that the civilian death toll from drone attacks is rising.
Africa.status: Sudanese army claim relayed by Addis Standard; no Ethiopian government response found in posts checked; not independently verified; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen kill at least 37 civilians travelling to a market near Téra, Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.location: Near Téra (village of Tillim), Tillabéri region, western Niger
Africa.summary: Several regional and international outlets report that unidentified gunmen killed at least 37 civilians on Thursday, Nov. 12, ambushing residents of the village of Tillim on their way to the weekly market near Téra, close to the borders with Mali and Burkina Faso. Mwanzo TV, citing local sources, says the dead include members of a local self-defence group escorting them. No official statement or claim of responsibility was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Multiple outlets citing local sources; no official statement found in posts checked; attackers unidentified; AFP now reports, citing local sources, that armed men killed at least 37 civilians in an ambush in western Niger near Burkina Faso and Mali; still no Nigerien government statement found; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Diplomatic sources tell Addis Standard that clashes are escalating near Badme on the Ethiopia–Eritrea border as residents flee
Africa.summary: Addis Standard cites two diplomatic sources saying intelligence reports over the past three days indicate clashes around the Badme front, with the latest engagements more intense than the low-intensity confrontations previously monitored. The sources mention drone strikes, and the outlet says residents are fleeing bombardment.
Africa.status: Early reports from anonymous diplomatic sources via an established Ethiopian outlet; no official statement from either government found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenyan detectives arrest three after recovering grenades and ammunition from a house in Tassia, Nairobi
Africa.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations says an intelligence-led operation in Tassia, Embakasi, found a bag of explosive devices and ammunition and led to three arrests. Citizen TV (cbs_ke) reports 15 grenades of different types and 16 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition were recovered, and that investigations into their intended use are ongoing.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (DCI Kenya); intended use under investigation; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Eight-storey building under construction collapses near the SGR terminus in Syokimau, Kenya; death toll reports range from three to six
Africa.location: Syokimau (Mombasa Road, near the SGR terminus), Machakos County, Kenya
Africa.summary: State broadcaster KBC reports three people died and five were rescued alive after an eight-storey building under construction collapsed in Syokimau on Friday morning. Other posts say six people were confirmed dead and five taken to hospital. The Star says the Kenya Red Cross is working with other emergency teams on search and rescue.
Africa.status: Early reports; death toll varies between three (KBC) and six (other posts); search and rescue ongoing; cause not officially confirmed; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Gunmen ambush SPLM delegates returning from party primaries in Mundri, South Sudan; at least two killed

Africa.summary: Gunmen ambushed a group of SPLM delegates travelling from Lui in Mundri East to Mundri West after party primaries on Thursday evening. SSEM TV reports at least two killed, including former SSBC journalist and parliamentary nominee Veronica Lucy Gordon, one critically injured and several missing. Africa_lix reports two wounded and several delegates fled into the bush.
Africa.status: Early reports; attackers unidentified; casualty details differ slightly between sources; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Guinea's government says 10 killed and 13 injured in clashes with security forces over an artisanal gold-mining ban near Siguiri
Africa.summary: RFI Afrique reports that a protest against the crackdown on artisanal gold mining broke out on Nov. 11 at Bouré-Balato, a major mining site about 20 km from Siguiri, and turned into clashes with defence and security forces. RFI gives no precise toll but says many sources report several deaths. A post attributed to AFP puts the toll at 10 killed; that figure was not confirmed by an AFP post found in this sweep.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (Guinea's Ministry of Territorial Administration, as reported by The Straits Times and wire summaries): 10 killed, 13 injured; clashes followed barricades on public roads in the northeast gold-producing region; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Safaricom USSD services fail across Kenya; Safaricom Care says it is looking into the issue
Africa.summary: Multiple Kenyan accounts report Safaricom USSD codes, including *444# and *544# used for bundles and balance checks, not working on the evening of Nov. 12 local time. Safaricom Care told a customer it is looking into the USSD issue and pointed users to the MyOne app and website. Whether M-Pesa payments were affected was not confirmed in posts checked.
Africa.status: Company acknowledged (Safaricom Care reply); scope and cause not stated; no restoration notice found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Ethiopian Orthodox Church says armed men killed at least 60 Christians in Ethiopia's Arsi zone
Africa.summary: i24NEWS reports that armed men went door to door in Arsi and killed at least 60 Christians, citing the Orthodox Church, and says thousands are fleeing. Another post reports more than 50 Orthodox Christians killed in an attack on a village in the Arsi region, following attacks it says killed at least 60 last month, so the figures may describe different attacks. The attackers have not been identified, and no Ethiopian government statement was found in posts checked.
Africa.status: Church figures reported by i24NEWS; figures vary across reports; no government confirmation or independent casualty count found in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Attack in Cantine-Aloya in eastern DR Congo reportedly kills 66 civilians, including three health workers; WHO warns of impact on Ebola response
Africa.summary: A post citing the World Health Organization says 66 civilians, including three health workers, were killed in an attack in Cantine-Aloya, and three health facilities were looted and burned. Reuters Africa separately reports Africa's top public health agency saying attacks on health workers and facilities are increasingly hindering efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo that has killed more than 5,400 people. The 66 figure was not confirmed by a primary WHO or UN post in posts checked.
Africa.status: Single-source casualty figure; broader attacks on health facilities reported by Reuters; awaiting WHO or UN primary confirmation; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Armed thugs attack opposition NDC town hall meeting in Lagos, Nigeria
Africa.summary: TheCable reports thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones attacked supporters of the opposition Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos on Thursday (Nov. 12). News Central TV says party members repelled the assault and one suspect was apprehended. A commentator relaying News Central TV says vehicles were destroyed and shots were fired into the air, and NDC supporters blame ruling-party (APC) thugs, which is unverified.
Africa.status: Early media reports (TheCable, News Central TV); no police statement or casualty figures found in posts checked; the event was to feature Peter Obi; News Central TV says the meeting continued after extra security was put in place and Peter Obi arrived; a post relaying local reports says Lagos police have opened an investigation and the House of Representatives set up a committee on political violence (not yet confirmed by an official police account in posts checked); carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: ADF attacks reportedly kill at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory, Ituri, DR Congo
Africa.location: Mambasa territory, Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
Africa.summary: Civil-society monitors say Islamic State-affiliated ADF rebels killed at least 22 civilians across eight communities in Mambasa territory between Tuesday and Wednesday (Nov. 10–11) and abducted at least 10 people, according to posts from Salone Messenger and NewsTongue. The attacks come amid the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo.
Africa.status: Early reports citing civil-society monitors; no Congolese army or government statement found on X in posts checked; CGTN Africa, citing humanitarian and security sources quoted by AFP, reports at least 44 civilians killed this week in a series of attacks by Islamic State-linked ADF fighters across northeastern DR Congo; it is unclear how much of that count overlaps with the Mambasa figures; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Fire and explosion at Sirte Oil Company gas complex in Marsa Brega, Libya, kills one worker; production unaffected
Africa.summary: Libya's National Oil Corporation says one worker was killed and four injured after a fire triggered an explosion at Sirte Oil Company's gas complex in Marsa Brega on Wednesday (Nov. 11), but gas and crude production was unaffected, Reuters and Arab News report. CGTN Europe says the NOC attributes it to an explosion in a fuel gas line and that the fire was contained.
Africa.status: Official statement issued (NOC); fire contained; appears accidental, no indication of an attack in posts checked; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Casablanca power outage — power restored; Moroccan outlets attribute it to wind gusts and storms (Storm Charles), and L'Economiste cites an incident on very-high-voltage lines
Africa.location: Casablanca and Nouaceur province (Bouskoura, Dar Bouazza), Morocco
Africa.summary: A large power outage hit many Casablanca neighborhoods and nearby localities on Wednesday afternoon (Nov. 11), starting around 5 p.m. local time, according to Yabiladi, Le Desk, Maroc Hebdo and state broadcaster SNRT. Medi1 TV reports wind gusts and storms caused the outage, L'Economiste reports an incident on very-high-voltage lines, and Le360 says power was fully restored around 9 p.m. in the affected neighborhoods, attributing the outage to Storm Charles. State news agency MAP and SNRT, citing prefecture sources, reported power restored in several zones earlier in the evening.
Africa.status: Power reported restored (fully, per Le360); regional utility SRM Casablanca-Settat issued an official statement (relayed by Medias24 and Maroc Hebdo); cause attributed to weather and a very-high-voltage line incident by multiple outlets; the earlier cyberattack hypothesis is not supported by any official source in posts checked; situation appears stabilized, can move to routine coverage; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.location: Manso Keniago (Amansie South District), Ashanti Region, Ghana

Africa.location: Hagarsu, Arabia Road, Mandera County, Kenya
Africa.summary: Reuters, citing police and a senior regional official, reports eight people — two police reservists, five construction workers and a driver — were killed Tuesday in northeast Kenya near the Somali border in an attack by suspected al-Shabaab militants. Kahawa Tungu and Nairobi News, citing police, place the ambush at Hagarsu along Arabia Road in Mandera County, targeting workers on the Arabia–Lafey road construction project. Africa.status: UN agency figure via Reuters; ongoing displacement; carried forward from 4:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Africa.location: Mogadishu to Barawe corridor, Lower Shabelle, Somalia
Africa.summary: Somali Guardian reports a Ugandan military convoy of more than 70 vehicles took over a week to travel from Mogadishu to Barawe as part of the withdrawal of remaining Ugandan troops, delayed by al-Shabaab attacks. Africa.title: CONTINUATION: Kenya Red Cross says Moyale border clashes in Ethiopia have displaced more than 50,000 people
Africa.summary: Voice of Horn reports Kenya Red Cross regional head Malik Adan says clashes around Ethiopia's Moyale area have displaced more than 50,000 people, many into northern Kenya, with shortages of food, shelter and bedding. South America.title: UPDATE: Remedios de Escalada (Lanús) gas explosion — five remain critical with severe burns, new gas leaks found and search of rubble continues for a missing MetroGAS worker
South America.location: Coronel Beltrán and Del Valle Iberlucea, Remedios de Escalada, Lanús, Buenos Aires province, Argentina

That claim is not independently confirmed. Earlier official maritime advisories still stand: UKMTO warnings 199-26 and 200-26, and JMIC’s note of two attacks on vessels in the latest reporting period. The IRGC’s earlier claim that three tankers exploded and burned also remains unconfirmed independently.

Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; The Economic Times reports US flights resuming after the ground stop was lifted, with officials ruling out a cyberattack; RT India (Russian state media) cites 4,000+ cancellations and 10,000+ delays; stabilizing, residual disruption expected; carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Europe.status: Single established outlet found on X; no injuries reported; no Garda statement found; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Europe.title: CONTINUATION: Storm Charles — Portugal shuts schools and non-essential public services Wednesday; Web Summit day cancelled, UEFA youth matches postponed, Madeira flights cancelled
Europe.summary: Portugal announced the closure of schools and non-essential public services on Nov. 11 as Storm Charles brings red wind warnings, according to Itatiaia and elsalvador.com; elsalvador.com also reports the Web Summit conference was cancelled. UEFA postponed youth club and national-team matches scheduled in Portugal for Nov. 11, per FredLine. The UK Met Office had warned of strong winds followed by heavy rain across Madeira, Portugal and Spain, with flight disruption already reported in Madeira.
Europe.status: Government closure measures reported by multiple outlets; red warnings in place; claims of a formal "state of emergency" come only from individual accounts and are unconfirmed; no casualty reports found yet; Reuters reports Portugal cancelled more than 200 flights and shut schools as the storm hit; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drone strike on a house in Proletarsky, Belgorod region, kills three, Russian regional officials say
Russia.location: Proletarsky, Rakitnoye district, Belgorod region, Russia
Russia.summary: SOTA, citing the Belgorod regional operational headquarters, reports a drone hit a private house in the settlement of Proletarsky, killing a married couple and their 24-year-old daughter and injuring another man. It also reports injuries from drone attacks in Shebekino and the village of Rzhevka.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Russian regional authorities, relayed); not independently verified; no Ukrainian comment found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drone strike sets warehouses on fire in Vyshhorod, just north of Kyiv
Russia.summary: WarTranslated reports a large fire in Vyshhorod near Kyiv after a drone strike on Saturday morning. A second account reports warehouses are on fire after the strike as attacks continued into the morning.
Russia.status: Early reports; casualties and official Ukrainian regional statement not found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, injure more than 50, including eight children; a rescuer clearing rubble is killed
Russia.summary: A Russian strike on Friday damaged two five-storey apartment buildings in Zaporizhzhia, causing fires, and rescuers freed people trapped in their apartments. Ukraine's State Emergency Service says 30 people were injured, including six children. Kyiv Post reports Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed two people on Friday, including a 17-year-old boy.
Russia.status: Official figures issued (Ukraine's State Emergency Service, as relayed by United24); search-and-rescue reported completed; a CGTN Europe post citing Ukrainian reports puts the injured at 50, which is not confirmed; Kyiv Independent now reports 50 injured, including eight children, and says a Cobra emergency-service rescuer was killed when a concrete slab fell on him while clearing debris, citing local authorities; Euromaidan Press, citing the Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration, says the Nov. 13 strikes killed two people and injured more than 50, and Anton Gerashchenko puts the dead at three including the rescuer; death counts differ slightly between sources; Ukraine Review reports 29 of those injured remain under medical care, six in serious condition, including six children aged 10 to 17; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Overnight Ukrainian drone attacks hit Rostov region and the Samara oil pumping station; Rostov-on-Don declares an emergency regime
Russia.location: Rostov-on-Don and Aksay district (Rostov region); Samara region, Russia
Russia.summary: NEXTA reports more than 120 drones attacked Russia's Rostov region on the night of Nov. 13, sparking a fire at a 1,500-square-metre warehouse in Aksay district and setting an industrial facility and three cars on fire in Rostov-on-Don. Sota reports Rostov-on-Don's mayor declared an emergency regime on streets where homes were damaged, saying nine apartment buildings were damaged and 114 houses were left without heat. The Insider reports the Samara regional governor confirmed a drone attack on an industrial enterprise, which monitoring channels identify as the Transneft-operated Samara oil pumping station (LPDS).
Russia.status: Official regional statements reported (Rostov governor and mayor, Samara governor); extent of damage at the Samara station not confirmed; separate from the Volgograd refinery strike logged below; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones strike the Volgograd oil refinery, setting fires; governor says four killed and two injured
Russia.summary: Multiple posts with video, including Liveuamap, report a drone attack on the Lukoil-operated Volgograd oil refinery on the evening of Nov. 12, with fires on the plant's grounds; one post says the extent of damage remains unconfirmed. A separate post relays Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin as saying more than 50 drones headed for Moscow were destroyed in about 90 minutes. Russian-source claims of 750 or more drones launched overall have not been verified.
Russia.status: Early reports with video from multiple accounts; no Volgograd regional or Lukoil statement found in posts checked; damage and casualties unconfirmed; a post citing ASTRA says reader photos show fires inside the refinery complex and that regional governor Andrei Bocharov confirmed fires at an unnamed enterprise in Volgograd's southern industrial zone, attributing them to falling drone debris; Kyiv Independent reports the mass drone attack on Moscow grounded flights at the region's airports, with Mayor Sobyanin claiming over a hundred drones shot down; claims that the refinery halted operations remain unconfirmed; a further post with video says the refinery was still burning after a lengthy drone attack, with several fires visible; Volgograd Governor Andrei Bocharov says four people, described as workers in the city's southern industrial zone, were killed and two injured in the overnight drone attack (TV Rain; Al Arabiya citing Reuters); Russia's Defense Ministry claimed 1,198 drones downed overnight over Russian regions and Crimea, per TV Rain; independent outlets report queues at Volgograd gas stations; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car explodes while driving in southern Moscow, seriously injuring the driver; Russian media say the car belonged to commentator Sergey Zavorotny
Russia.location: Kirovogradskaya Street, Chertanovo district, Moscow, Russia
Russia.summary: A car exploded while being driven on Kirovogradskaya Street in Moscow's Chertanovo district on the morning of Nov. 13, throwing the driver onto the road. Russian media, cited by NEXTA and WarTranslated, say the car belonged to Sergey Zavorotny, a pro-Kremlin commentator and former press secretary to ex-Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov; OSINTtechnical reports he was seriously injured. It comes a day after a car bomb killed a Russian Air Force colonel in St. Petersburg.
Russia.status: Early reports; cause under investigation; one Russian outlet cited a preliminary suspicion of a gas-system malfunction; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; The Washington Post now describes it as a car bombing that seriously injured a former adviser to ex-Ukrainian PM Mykola Azarov who became a pro-Kremlin commentator in Russia; no official Russian statement or claim of responsibility found in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: UPDATE: Overnight Russian drone attack on Ukraine — 117 drones launched, strikes at 24 locations; at least two killed, medical facility hit in Kyiv
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russia launched 117 drones overnight, including 63 jet-powered drones; 80 were intercepted or suppressed, but strikes were recorded at 24 locations and at least two people were killed. A Ukrainian outlet reports a 17-year-old was killed in Zaporizhzhia and that a night strike on a medical facility in Kyiv injured one person, with seven people freed and 30 evacuated.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Ukrainian government communications center); casualty details from a single media account; First Squawk reports Ukraine's deputy energy minister says the overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure caused power outages in 12 regions; Ukraine's Foreign Ministry says the overnight Russian strikes killed two people and injured at least 14 across Ukraine, including a strike that destroyed a private house in Odesa (two killed, five injured) and an attack on an apartment building in Rivne (six injured); TVP World reports Ukrainian authorities count at least nine killed and 61 wounded in the overnight attacks across multiple regions, including three wounded and 30 evacuated in Kyiv; this is higher than the Foreign Ministry's earlier count of two killed and 14 injured, and the regions covered may differ; Ukrinform reports a Russian attack on an energy facility in Odesa region left nearly 50,000 consumers without power

Russia.summary: Reuters reports that Finland's military said it detected "a strike" on a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea a day earlier but that the security situation in the area remained stable. Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car bomb kills a Russian Air Force colonel in Shushary, St. Petersburg
Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. Russian media cited by these accounts identify him as the chief navigator of the 6th Air Force and Air Defense Army, but he has not been named. It is the second similar under-car bombing of an officer in the same area since late August.
Russia.status: Corroborated by multiple outlets (Novaya Gazeta Europe, The Straits Times; Russia's Investigative Committee cited by journalist Christopher Miller); colonel's name not officially confirmed; suspect reports come from Russian media only; no claim of responsibility; The Kyiv Independent and Xinhua cite St. Petersburg's Investigative Committee saying a serviceman was killed when his car exploded in the Pushkinsky district (Shushary) and a murder case has been opened; CGTN Europe reports a Russian serviceman was killed when his SUV was destroyed by an explosion in the Pushkinsky District, with a nearby bus also damaged; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight — one woman killed in a Solomianskyi high-rise; State Emergency Service says two rescuers killed in Kyiv region
Russia.location: Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast (Bila Tserkva, Irpin areas), Ukraine
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent says its journalists heard multiple explosions in Kyiv around 1 a.m. local time on Thursday (Nov. 12; about 6 p.m. ET Wednesday), shortly after Ukraine's Air Force warned that missiles were targeting the capital. OSINT account AMK Mapping says at least 11 missiles were used, including about five Iskander-Ms, and lists an Epicentr shopping center in northern Kyiv and the eastern industrial zone among the targets, with further strikes in the Bila Tserkva and Irpin areas. Journalist Oliver Carroll also reported ballistic strikes on Kyiv.
Russia.status: Official statements issued (Kyiv City Military Administration; State Emergency Service as relayed by CGTN Europe): one killed and five injured in Kyiv city, two rescuers killed in Kyiv region; Russian MoD target claims unverified; Ukrinform, citing Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko, says one person was killed and seven injured in the strike on the residential building, with fire on the third to sixth floors; Euromaidan Press says the woman killed was 44; ZMiST reports the overnight attack caused damage across eight Ukrainian regions, mainly energy and transport infrastructure, including a power generation facility in Zaporizhzhia and high-voltage substations in Odesa and Rivne regions; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones attack the Omsk oil refinery in Siberia for hours; large fire reported at Russia's largest refinery
Russia.location: Omsk, Omsk Oblast, Russia (Gazprom Neft Omsk refinery)
Russia.summary: Russian local channels and multiple OSINT and media accounts report a prolonged Ukrainian drone attack on Omsk on Nov. 11, with the Gazprom Neft refinery named as the target and air defense activity lasting more than two hours. NOELreports, Liveuamap, Exilenova+ and NEXTA report the refinery is on fire, with footage of a very large blaze. The refinery is roughly 2,500 km from the front line.
Russia.status: Multiple independent accounts and footage; no official Russian statement on damage found in posts checked; Hromadske reports the Omsk regional governor confirmed a drone attack on the region but did not acknowledge a refinery strike; damage remains unclear; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Hackers deface Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform and hijack its X account
Russia.summary: Ukrainian state news agency Ukrinform was hit by a cyberattack on Nov. 11: hackers defaced its website and altered its official X profile, replacing its name and imagery with anti-Ukrainian propaganda, Hromadske reports. The website was taken offline for maintenance as Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities investigated. Hungary's MTI says Ukrinform director general Serhiy Cheravatyi disclosed the attack.
Russia.status: Confirmed by Ukrinform's director general per MTI; investigation under way; no attribution announced in posts checked; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a crowded market in Chornomorsk, Odesa region, kills three and injures 11
Russia.summary: A Russian strike hit a market in central Chornomorsk on Nov. 11, killing three people and injuring 11, according to regional authorities cited by NOELreports and Ukrainian outlets. Hromadske Radio says nine of the injured were hospitalized, four in serious condition, and trading stalls were damaged and windows blown out. Early reports gave one dead before the toll rose.
Russia.status: Regional authorities report; toll rose from one to three killed during the morning; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

links.label: New Voice of Ukraine on X

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro kills three and injures four
Russia.summary: Suspilne, citing regional military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha, reports a Russian strike hit a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro, killing two people, injuring at least four and starting a fire. Hromadske Radio later reported the toll rose to three, with businesses and a private home also damaged and four men hospitalized, two in serious condition. CGTN Europe, citing Ukraine's health service, reports three killed and five injured across Dnipropetrovsk region during the day.
Russia.status: Official (regional military administration) figures relayed by Ukrainian outlets; emergency services at the scene; facility not named; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian missile and drone strikes target Odesa Oblast bridges and 330 kV substations, plus substations in Kharkiv and Chernihiv, OSINT mapper reports
Russia.location: Odesa Oblast (Mayaky, Zatoka, Artsyz), Kharkiv and Chernihiv, Ukraine
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports a large combined Russian attack on Odesa Oblast overnight using cruise missiles, glide bombs and drones, targeting the Mayaky and Zatoka road bridges that link southern Odesa Oblast to the rest of Ukraine, as well as 330 kV substations in Artsyz and the "Podilska" substation. It says at least four cruise missiles were shot down and two flew briefly through Moldovan airspace. The same account reports fires in Kharkiv and Chernihiv after strikes on 110 kV substations.
Russia.status: Early reports; single OSINT mapping source; damage and outages not yet confirmed by Ukrainian officials or utilities on X; Kharkiv and Chernihiv substation strikes echoed by other OSINT accounts (one says one person injured in Kharkiv); still no Ukrainian official or utility statement found on X; First Squawk relays the Odesa governor saying energy targets were hit overnight; bne IntelliNews reports Russian strikes cut power to 135,000 in Odesa region; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters says Russia pounds Ukraine's power grid as talks open in Abu Dhabi; Dnipro and Kyiv supply remains especially difficult
Russia.location: Dnipropetrovsk region (Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske and other communities), Ukraine; also Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions
Russia.summary: Ukrinform reports Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said the power supply situation remains especially difficult in Kyiv and Dnipro. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.
Russia.status: Ongoing grid attacks per Reuters; restoration continuing; no current national outage total given; Ukraine's Energy Ministry says new power outages have been reported in nine regions and four energy workers were injured in a Russian attack in the Poltava region; repair crews are working to restore power; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Kryvyi Rih — AMK Mapping says two 330 kV substations hit by at least 16 Geran-2 drones; Reuters confirms partial blackout
Russia.summary: A massed Russian drone attack on energy infrastructure left parts of Kryvyi Rih without power, according to city official Oleksandr Vilkul. Apartment buildings, schools and kindergartens were damaged. Water and sewage services are being stabilized with generators, but heating will be harder to restore. AMK Mapping says at least 16 Geran-2 drones were used and that the "Pivdenna" and "Hirnycha" 330 kV substations on the city's southern outskirts were hit.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (city official Oleksandr Vilkul); Reuters reports the outage; substation details from OSINT mapping account, not officially confirmed; casualty figures not reported; Reuters headline reconfirmed this window; carried forward from 6:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Leningrad governor confirms fire in Ust-Luga port area and emergency substation shutdown during drone attack; says 146 drones intercepted overnight
Russia.summary: Leningrad region governor Alexander Drozdenko said a fire broke out in the Ust-Luga port area during an overnight Ukrainian drone attack and that a substation in the port zone went into emergency shutdown. He said 146 drones were intercepted over the region as of 7:30 a.m. local time and that there was no information on casualties. Earlier OSINT footage showed the oil terminal burning.

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters says Ukrainian strikes have cut Russia's oil refining capacity by about 30%; fuel purchase limits spread to St. Petersburg and Leningrad region
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent and Novaya Gazeta Europe, citing Reuters and two industry sources, report renewed Ukrainian attacks since late October have cut Russian refining capacity by about 30%, disrupting nine of Russia's 35 major refineries over the past week, including plants in Ryazan and Yaroslavl, per Meduza. SOTA, citing Bumaga, reports Rosneft stations in St. Petersburg have capped purchases since Nov. 8, and Novaya Gazeta Europe reports fuel limits returning in Leningrad region.

RBC-Ukraine and Ukrinform, citing media reports, say drones targeted a plant in Novgorod region that services military aircraft.

Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent, citing the IAEA, reports a drone strike killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and that in a separate incident an employee at the nearby Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant was also killed by a drone. Middle East.location: Kfar Tebnit and Barashit, Nabatieh area, southern Lebanon

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Large explosion reported at dawn in Zawtar al-Sharqiya, southern Lebanon, amid Israeli artillery shelling of nearby areas
Middle East.location: Zawtar al-Sharqiya, Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon

TheCable reports disruption across 74 countries and territories; not resolved; at about 6:11 AM ET Microsoft said recovery actions were completed across portions of affected infrastructure with traffic gradually restored and mailbox access improving; at about 7:09 AM ET it reported encouraging recovery progress across a growing portion of affected infrastructure, with some intermittent issues continuing and the 48-hour email timeout still in place; Times Radio's technology editor says it does not look like a cyberattack; at about 8:32 AM ET Microsoft reported broader recovery in North America, sustained improvement across much of Europe and encouraging signals in Asia Pacific; Europe.summary: Lithuania issued red air-attack warnings for several southern districts, including Druskininkai and Lazdijai, after unidentified objects, most likely drones, entered from Belarus, and NATO jets were scrambled from Šiauliai. Mario Nawfal, citing Lithuania's National Crisis Management Centre, says four objects were tracked, three of them in Latvian airspace, and that they were likely Ukrainian drones headed for St. Petersburg. Several accounts cite broadcaster LRT as saying Kaunas Airport suspended operations. America.summary: The FAA grounded departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centers, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety," AP reports. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a communication issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, according to CBS News. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage, said there is currently no reason to suspect a national security threat, and told CBS News that investigators can't rule anything out yet. Fox News reports more than 7,000 flights delayed or canceled, and CBS reports flights diverting as airports reach capacity.
America.status: Official statements issued; ground stop lifted, recovery under way. AP and CNN report the FAA said departures can resume; OSINTdefender relays that the FAA Command Center canceled the stop as of 8:19 p.m. ET. At a White House briefing, Transportation Sec. Duffy said older network switches and routers became overloaded and sent bad data, that not all telecom and radar systems were lost, and that recovery will take time, with some travelers likely sleeping in airports; DHS Sec. Mullin said there is no indication of a cyberattack and no connection to the Microsoft 365 outage. Al Jazeera English reported more than 4,000 cancellations and 10,000 delays while the stop was in effect. Viral posts claiming a massive Iranian cyberattack are contradicted by these officials and are not relied on. Situation stabilizing; monitoring can scale back unless the outage recurs; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found

America.title: CONTINUATION: Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Exchange Online and Teams; Microsoft says it may affect users in any region
America.location: United States and Canada; possibly worldwide
America.summary: Microsoft's 365 status account said it was investigating problems reaching Exchange Online mailboxes in the Americas, then said the issue may affect Microsoft 365 connectivity for users in any region. America.status: Official statement issued (Microsoft 365 Status, incidents EX1550543 and MO1550821); mitigation under way; no cause beyond elevated load given; Microsoft says no indication of malicious or cyber activity; Microsoft 365 Status says an alternative health-check method let a subset of affected servers return to service and it is applying the change more broadly while preparing automated recovery; partial recovery under way; Al Jazeera English says the outage hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot with about 130,000 Downdetector problem reports at its peak, and that Microsoft said servers unexpectedly went offline; recovery under way; Reuters says Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams and other apps stayed disrupted for thousands of users for more than five hours on Thursday and that the outage also hit connectors used by OpenAI's and Anthropic's AI services; CNN says the outage continued for much of the workday; as of about 11:37 PM ET Microsoft said it was observing partial recovery in regions where traffic changes were applied, and at about midnight ET said it was still working to address a "current blocker" and return infrastructure to a healthy state (MO1550821); not fully resolved; at about 1:12 AM ET Microsoft said it was still recovering frontend servers and applying traffic optimization to improve stability and capacity (MO1550821); Reuters reports Australia's spy agency and federal police were among organizations hit, with the Australian government triggering an agreement with Microsoft for priority restoration; not resolved; at about 2:44 AM ET Microsoft said its latest traffic optimization actions were improving stability and capacity and were being rolled out more broadly across affected regions as it seeks persistent recovery; AP says Microsoft is still struggling to restore services for companies and governments; EFE reports a Microsoft executive ruled out a cyberattack as the cause; a Kenyan commentator reports banks in several African countries warning customers of service interruptions; not resolved; at about 4:24 AM ET Microsoft reported early stabilization and capacity improvements and said it extended the email timeout to 48 hours to preserve delayed mail; at about 5:28 AM ET it said recovery actions are progressing in phases with incremental improvement in several workloads, but service health remains variable and capacity has not yet fully returned to baseline; TheCable reports disruption across 74 countries and territories; not resolved; at about 6:11 AM ET Microsoft said recovery actions were completed across portions of affected infrastructure with traffic gradually restored and mailbox access improving; at about 7:09 AM ET it reported encouraging recovery progress across a growing portion of affected infrastructure, with some intermittent issues continuing and the 48-hour email timeout still in place; Times Radio's technology editor says it does not look like a cyberattack; at about 8:32 AM ET Microsoft reported broader recovery in North America, sustained improvement across much of Europe and encouraging signals in Asia Pacific; at about 9:17 AM ET it said email queues were significantly reduced and approaching normal levels, with some users still seeing intermittent access issues or delayed mail (admin center incident MO1550821); at about 10:39 AM ET Microsoft 365 Status reported encouraging recovery and said there is no indication the outage resulted from malicious or cyber activity; a statement from Microsoft relayed by a Sky News correspondent attributes it to a bug introduced months ago by a network-gateway capacity upgrade, triggered by a network change on Thursday that caused a cascading failure, and says the bug has been addressed and customers and regions are being brought back online gradually; at about 1:05 PM ET Microsoft 365 Status reported broad recovery and stability, said the incident was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents, traced it to an issue from an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a recent network change, and said it is still restoring remaining customers and regions and will publish a post-incident report; situation appears to be stabilizing; carried forward from 10:15 PM ET, no newer change found
